_README: Signature registry for the Marg Report Router. ADDING A NEW REPORT TYPE IS A
DATA EDIT HERE -- no code change. Run 'marg_router.py --learn <file>' on a
sample and it prints a ready-to-paste block.
Matching rule: title_regex AND header must BOTH match, else the file is
refused (a partial match is never parsed). Unknown files are quarantined,
type          short code, becomes the archive folder name
variant       distinguishes layouts of the same report (DETAIL vs SUMMARY1)
title_regex   matched against the title row (case-insensitive)
header        expected column headers, in order; matched as a prefix
uploadable    true = a VERIFIED file is copied to the Outbox for sending
end_marker    optional text that must appear near the end (completeness)

signatures._comment: S205: the SUPPLIER/ITEM WISE purchase statement -- a THIRD purchase report, and the richest. PURCHASE_BILLWISE gives bill -> supplier -> date -> amount; PURCHASE_SUPPLIERWISE gives the supplier view; this gives the LINES INSIDE each bill, with batch, expiry, rate, discount and net rate. The three join on BILL. This is the Purchase Portal's (D335) real input.
signatures.end_marker_note: S205: MEASURED against all five real exports, not copied from the sibling signature. "GRAND TOTAL" -- which PURCHASE_SUPPLIERWISE uses -- matches 0 of 5 here, because in THIS layout Marg splits it across two cells ('GRAND' | 'TOTAL') and ends_with() searches cells, not rows. Copying it would have refused every real report. 'Digital Purchase' is Marg's own footer, the literal last line, so it is a true completeness signal; 'GRAND' also matches 5/5 but appears inside item descriptions in Indian pharma catalogues and would risk a FALSE GREEN on a truncated export. If Marg ever stops printing the footer these reports go to _REFUSED with the reason stated -- visible and recoverable by a rescan, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.
